interpretation.purpose: Coverage-expansion sources for candidate discovery and review of prediction-feature taxonomies.
interpretation.review_boundary: Review articles authorize search coverage and candidate discovery only. A candidate formula must still be verified against a named primary application or foundational mathematical source before final admission.
interpretation.association_boundary: Prediction or association with later citations is not evidence of causality, scientific quality, correctness, or innovation.

records.citation: Kousha K, Thelwall M (2024). Factors associating with or predicting more cited or higher quality journal articles: An Annual Review of Information Science and Technology (ARIST) paper. Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology 75:215-244.
records.finding: The review maps a wide range of article, reference, author, collaboration, journal, text, topic, design, and openness correlates of citations and quality, while emphasizing heterogeneity and limited causal evidence.
records.limitations: A review-level mention does not fix an article-level formula, timing boundary, or cross-field validity.

records.citation: Park G, Yi S (2026). Prediction of high-impact research: a historical review and research opportunities. Scientometrics 131:4001-4047.
records.study_type: peer-reviewed historical review with machine-assisted screening
records.finding: The review organizes high-impact prediction around scholarly visibility, radicality or disruptiveness, and structural network position, and calls for benchmark data and stronger reliability checks.
records.limitations: The authors report machine-assisted relevance screening and acknowledge subjectivity and the absence of formal inter-coder reliability in parts of the review process.

records.citation: Xia W, Li T, Li C (2023). A review of scientific impact prediction: tasks, features and methods. Scientometrics 128:543-585.
records.finding: The review surveys scientific-impact prediction tasks, feature categories, targets, models, and evaluation practices.
records.limitations: Coverage of a feature category is not primary validation of a construct or a frozen publication-time formula.

records.citation: Aiza WSN, Shuib L, Idris N, Normadhi NBA (2024). Features, techniques and evaluation in predicting articles' citations: a review from years 2010-2023. Scientometrics 129:1-29.
records.finding: The review catalogs feature classes, prediction techniques, datasets, horizons, and evaluation measures used from 2010 through 2023.
records.limitations: Included studies use heterogeneous outcomes, time windows, fields, and data leakage controls.

records.citation: Bai X, Zhang F, Liu J, Wang X, Xia F (2025). Revolutionizing scholarly impact: advanced evaluations, predictive models, and future directions. Artificial Intelligence Review 58:311.
records.finding: The review groups impact features into attribute, content, network, and temporal families and identifies feature availability and evaluation design as major constraints.
records.limitations: The taxonomy mixes publication-time predictors, early post-publication signals, outcomes, and contextual variables; every candidate requires a T0 audit.

records.citation: Robson BJ, Mousques A (2016). Can we predict citation counts of environmental modelling papers? Fourteen bibliographic and categorical variables predict less than 30% of the variability in citation counts. Environmental Modelling & Software 75:94-104.
formula_authorization: article-level bibliographic and categorical feature definitions reported in the study
records.finding: Fourteen bibliographic and categorical variables explained less than 30 percent of citation-count variability in the studied field.
records.limitations: Single field, observational outcome, and limited explained variance; not an innovation validation study.

records.citation: Fronzetti Colladon A, D'Angelo CA, Gloor PA (2020). Predicting the future success of scientific publications through social network and semantic analysis. Scientometrics 124:357-377.
records.study_type: primary network and semantic prediction study
records.finding: The study evaluates combined social-network and semantic features for predicting later publication success.
records.limitations: Prediction is not construct validation; exact timing and portability must be re-audited before reuse.

records.citation: Weihs L, Etzioni O (2017). Learning to Predict Citation-Based Impact Measures. 2017 ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries:1-10.
formula_authorization: publication-time feature definitions explicitly reported in the study
records.finding: The study learns to predict citation-based impact measures from scholarly-paper information.
records.limitations: Any early citation or post-publication feature in the original task is ineligible for the present T0 predictor set.

records.citation: Zhu H, Li S (2024). Instant prediction of scientific paper cited potential based on semantic and metadata features: Taking artificial intelligence field as an example. PLOS ONE 19:e0312945.
records.finding: The study evaluates semantic and metadata variables for instant prediction of cited potential in artificial intelligence.
records.limitations: One field and one prediction setting; cited potential is not the same construct as innovation or scientific quality.

records.citation: Ma A, Liu Y, Xu X, Dong T (2021). A deep-learning based citation count prediction model with paper metadata semantic features. Scientometrics 126:6803-6823.
formula_authorization: study-specific paper metadata and semantic feature representation
records.finding: The study combines paper metadata and semantic representations in a citation-count prediction model.
records.limitations: Deep representations require versioned training data and models, and predictive performance does not establish construct validity.
